key_insight: A generalized swimming formula shows how anisotropic and odd viscosity shape microswimmer motion while preserving the scallop theorem in linearly viscous fluids.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide microswimmer control and transport predictions in fluids with anisotropic or chiral viscous responses.
method: Model low-Reynolds-number flow with even and odd viscosity tensors.
Use the generalized Lorentz reciprocal theorem to establish Onsager–Casimir reciprocity for rigid-body resistance tensors.
Derive a swimming formula and analyze a spherical swimmer in an odd-viscous fluid.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs and a spherical-swimmer analysis showing that sufficiently strong shear destabilizes bimodal chirotactic alignment; no experimental validation is described.
watch_item: Applicability is limited to low-Reynolds-number, linearly viscous fluids; nonlinear rheology and inertial effects lie outside the stated framework.
paper_title: Swimming formula in a linearly viscous fluid with anisotropic and odd viscosity tensors at low Reynolds number
